import Accordion from "@components/Accordion.astro"; While most investors chase the latest property trends or debate office versus industrial investments, a quietly powerful sector has been delivering superior returns right under their noses. Large format retail properties — those sprawling warehouse-style stores where you buy everything from power tools to dining tables — have consistently outperformed the broader commercial property market. With average yields of 6.5% crushing other commercial property classes and backed by Australia's population boom, large format retail (LFR) offers something increasingly rare in today's market: genuine value combined with defensive characteristics. If you're looking for an investment that makes sense both on paper and in practice, it's time to take a closer look at this overlooked opportunity. ### What exactly is large format retail Think of large format retail as the practical cousin of traditional shopping centres. These are those massive warehouse-style buildings ranging from 1,000 to 10,000 square metres that house the stores you probably visit more often than you realise. You know these places well, even if you've never thought of them as investments. That weekend trip to Bunnings for garden supplies? Large format retail. Shopping for a new mattress at Harvey Norman? LFR again. Picking up office supplies at Officeworks or browsing furniture at Amart? All large format retail. ### The practical difference Unlike shopping centres with their enclosed malls, food courts, and complex tenant mixes, LFR properties focus on function over form. Picture individual warehouse stores arranged around shared parking areas — it's retail stripped back to basics, but that simplicity is exactly what makes it work so well. These buildings prioritise what matters most: accessibility, storage space, and operational efficiency. There's no expensive marble flooring or elaborate decorative features. Instead, you get high ceilings, wide aisles, and plenty of parking — exactly what you need when buying a washing machine or a week's worth of hardware supplies. This no-frills approach isn't just practical for shoppers; it's brilliant for investors. Lower construction costs mean higher initial yields, while the straightforward design attracts quality tenants seeking cost-effective retail space. ### Why the yields make investors pay attention Here's where LFR gets really interesting for your investment portfolio. In 2024, these properties delivered average yields of 6.5% — significantly ahead of CBD offices at 6%, regional shopping centres at 5.5%, and industrial warehouses at 5.4%. But this isn't just a one-year wonder. Over the past decade, LFR has averaged 7.46% yields compared to industrial properties at 5.84% and neighbourhood shopping centres at 6.14%. That's a meaningful difference that compounds significantly over time. #### Why these yields stay strong The secret lies in the tenants themselves. When Bunnings signs a lease, they're not planning to move anytime soon. These retailers invest heavily in store fit-outs, build customer loyalty in specific locations, and operate on long-term business strategies. This creates what investors love most: predictable, stable income streams. Plus, many LFR products fall into the "needs, not wants" category. You might delay buying a new car or holiday, but when your washing machine breaks or you need supplies for urgent home repairs, those purchases can't wait. This defensive characteristic helps protect rental income even when economic conditions tighten. In today's higher interest rate environment, finding genuine 6%+ yields from quality assets with established tenants represents genuine value that's increasingly hard to find elsewhere. ### Australia's population boom creates perfect conditions Here's where the LFR investment story gets compelling. Australia is experiencing one of the fastest population growth rates in the developed world, with over 15% growth expected between 2023 and 2033. That translates to 4.43 million new residents who all need somewhere to live and furnish their homes. #### The furniture and appliance connection Think about what happens when people move house or set up new homes. Every new migrant family represents multiple shopping trips to Harvey Norman, Bunnings, and similar stores over their first few years in Australia. The numbers are staggering: experts project an additional $45 billion in retail spending from migration-related demand over the next decade. That's $4.5 billion annually flowing through the exact types of stores that anchor LFR properties. #### Supply isn't keeping up Here's the kicker: while Australia's population has grown 15% over the past decade, retail space per person has actually declined from 2.3 square metres per person to under 2.1 square metres. We're literally running out of retail space relative to population growth. New LFR supply remains severely constrained. There's only 711,845 square metres of new space planned through 2026 — that's just 0.41 square metres per additional resident. Compare that to current levels, and you can see why existing LFR properties are becoming increasingly valuable. Land suitable for LFR development has become scarce, particularly in metropolitan areas where demand is strongest. Planning restrictions and competition from industrial users further limit new supply, creating scarcity value for existing properties. ### Investment market shows interesting trends The LFR investment market tells a fascinating story of changing investor behaviour and emerging opportunities. Transaction volumes peaked at $3.7 billion in 2022 before cooling to around $810 million in 2024. However, early 2025 activity suggests the market is finding its feet again. [How the broader commercial property market is performing](/articles/commercial-property-market-changes-drive-new-investment-patterns/). #### Private investors step up One of the most significant trends has been the shift toward private investment. In 2023, private buyers represented 66% of transactions, more than doubling from just 36% in 2020. This suggests institutional investors may have stepped back, creating opportunities for sophisticated private investors to acquire quality assets. The market has also developed what experts call a "flight to quality" mentality. Investors increasingly focus on premium assets with strong anchor tenants, strategic locations, and modern facilities. These top-tier properties have become tightly held, with owners recognising their long-term value and reluctant to sell. #### Scarcity creates value With only 332 LFR centres operating nationally across 5.345 million square metres of space, this represents one of the most tightly held commercial property sectors. - faqTitle2: Can I use my superannuation to buy an investment property?
- faqAnswer2: Self-managed super funds (SMSFs) can buy investment properties under strict rules. The property must meet the sole purpose test of providing retirement benefits. SMSFs cannot buy properties from related parties and must maintain arm's length management. Seek professional advice before using super for property investment.
- faqTitle3: What insurance do property investors need?
- faqAnswer3: Landlord insurance protects against tenant-related risks like damage and missed rent. Building insurance covers structural issues and natural disasters. Consider income protection insurance if relying on employment income to service loans. Public liability insurance guards against injury claims from tenants or visitors.
- faqTitle4: How does the ATO view short-term rental investments?
- faqAnswer4: Properties rented through platforms like Airbnb face different tax treatment than traditional rentals. The ATO requires detailed income and expense records. GST may apply if turnover exceeds thresholds. Capital gains tax calculations change if mixing personal use with short-term letting.
- faqTitle5: What impact does zoning have on investment properties?
- faqAnswer5: Local council zoning affects how properties can be used and developed. Some zones allow subdivision or multi-dwelling construction, increasing potential returns. Others restrict modifications or rental types. Check zoning before buying and monitor proposed changes that could affect property values.

Land availability represents Melbourne's most significant advantage. The city offers larger, more accessible industrial land parcels suitable for hyperscale data centre development. Sydney's mature market has resulted in limited suitable sites, driving up land costs and constraining development options. During this period, 18.9MW of new capacity became operational, bringing total live IT capacity to 757.0MW. - faqAnswer1: Melbourne's housing market ranking has significantly shifted since the COVID-19 pandemic. In March 2020, Melbourne had the second-highest median dwelling value among Australian capital cities. However, by August 2024, Melbourne's ranking dropped to sixth-lowest, with a median dwelling value of $776,000. This change reflects broader shifts in Australia's property market, influenced by factors such as demographic patterns, housing supply, and interstate migration trends.
- faqTitle2: What factors have contributed to the widening gap between Sydney and Melbourne's median dwelling values?
- faqAnswer2: The gap between Sydney and Melbourne's median dwelling values has widened to 52.1%, the largest difference since June 1999. This widening gap can be attributed to several factors, including: 1) Victoria's higher rate of dwelling completions compared to other states, 2) differences in net interstate migration trends, with Melbourne experiencing departures due to strict social distancing restrictions, 3) variations in housing composition, with Melbourne having a higher proportion of multi-unit dwellings, and 4) changing demographic patterns influencing housing demand across Australian cities.
- faqTitle3: How does housing composition affect median dwelling values in Australian capital cities?
- faqAnswer3: Housing composition significantly influences median dwelling values in Australian capital cities. For instance, in Melbourne, about 33% of housing stock is in the multi-unit sector, compared to only 16% in Adelaide and Perth. This higher proportion of apartments and units in Melbourne tends to lower the overall median dwelling value. As cities like Perth and Adelaide face increasing affordability challenges and infrastructure costs, they may shift towards higher-density housing, potentially impacting their future median dwelling values and market rankings.
- faqTitle4: What role has interstate migration played in shaping Australia's property market since 2020?
- faqAnswer4: Interstate migration has played a crucial role in shaping Australia's property market since 2020. Melbourne, in particular, experienced a 'push' factor due to strict and extended social distancing restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic. This led to increased departures from Melbourne, benefiting cities like Brisbane, Perth, and Adelaide. These migration patterns have contributed to shifting property values and demand across different capital cities, influencing their relative market positions and median dwelling values.
- faqTitle5: How might future urban planning trends affect housing markets in Perth and Adelaide?
- faqAnswer5: Future urban planning trends in Perth and Adelaide may significantly affect their housing markets. As affordability becomes more stretched and state governments aim to reduce costs associated with sprawling infrastructure, there's likely to be a renewed focus on establishing higher densities in these cities. This shift towards more compact urban development could lead to changes in housing composition, potentially increasing the proportion of multi-unit dwellings. Such changes may impact median dwelling values, affordability, and the overall character of these housing markets in the coming years.

- faqTitle1: What is debtor finance and how does it help Australian businesses manage cash flow?
- faqAnswer1: Debtor finance, also known as invoice finance in Australia, is a financial solution that allows businesses to access funds tied up in outstanding invoices. It helps Australian businesses manage cash flow by providing immediate working capital based on unpaid customer invoices. This enables companies to bridge the gap between delivering goods or services and receiving payment, ensuring smoother operations and the ability to meet financial obligations without waiting for customer payments.
- faqTitle2: How can Australian businesses evaluate customer creditworthiness to reduce debtor finance risks?
- faqAnswer2: Australian businesses can evaluate customer creditworthiness to reduce debtor finance risks by conducting thorough credit checks and assessing payment history. Utilise credit reporting agencies to gain insights into customers' financial health and payment behaviour. Implement stringent credit assessment processes to identify high-risk customers who may default on payments. This evaluation helps businesses make informed decisions about which invoices to finance, thereby minimising the risk of bad debts and protecting their financial stability.
- faqTitle3: Why is diversifying the customer base important for Australian companies using debtor finance?
- faqAnswer3: Diversifying the customer base is crucial for Australian companies using debtor finance because it spreads credit exposure across multiple clients, reducing the impact of any single customer defaulting. Relying on a small number of customers can be risky, as financial difficulties or payment delays from key clients can significantly affect cash flow. By building a diverse customer portfolio, businesses enhance their stability, minimise risk, and create a more resilient financial foundation, ensuring a steadier cash flow through debtor finance arrangements.
- faqTitle4: What strategies can Australian businesses use to effectively monitor outstanding invoices in debtor finance?
- faqAnswer4: Australian businesses can effectively monitor outstanding invoices in debtor finance by implementing several strategies. Regularly review accounts receivable and track payment status using automated invoicing and payment tracking systems. Establish a systematic approach for following up on overdue invoices to ensure timely collection. Promptly address late payments to reduce the risk of prolonged cash flow issues. By maintaining vigilant oversight of outstanding invoices, businesses can optimise their debtor finance arrangements and maintain a healthy financial position.
- faqTitle5: How important is communication in managing debtor finance risks for Australian companies?
- faqAnswer5: Communication is crucial in managing debtor finance risks for Australian companies. Maintain open lines of communication with both clients and your debtor finance provider. Regularly update your provider on any changes in customer credit status or payment behaviour. Clear communication ensures all parties are informed and can respond proactively to potential issues. Additionally, clearly communicate credit terms, including payment deadlines and late payment penalties, to customers. This transparency sets clear expectations and provides a solid basis for enforcing payment agreements, ultimately reducing debtor finance risks.

As a result, investors and developers may need to adapt their strategies to align with these technological trends and changing space requirements.
- faqTitle3: How is the return to brick-and-mortar shopping affecting the commercial property landscape?
- faqAnswer3: The return to brick-and-mortar shopping is having a significant impact on the commercial property landscape. Consumers are increasingly returning to physical stores, particularly for food and groceries. This shift could bring stock back to stores, potentially energizing retail assets across the country. As a result, the demand for large distribution facilities may decrease, while retail properties could see increased interest. This changing consumer behavior is prompting a reevaluation of investment strategies in both the industrial and retail property sectors.
- faqTitle4: What challenges is the industrial property sector currently facing in Australia?
- faqAnswer4: The industrial property sector in Australia is facing several challenges. The past 18 months have seen a slowdown in large industrial transactions, with changing financing costs contributing to rising yields and some land value declines across the country. Despite persistently low vacancies, rents have leveled off, and new supply has been limited due to high construction costs. These factors are dampening investment demand. Additionally, the plateauing of online retail growth and technological advancements in space utilization are raising questions about future demand for large industrial facilities.
- faqTitle5: How might the changing dynamics in online retail and industrial property affect investment strategies?
- faqAnswer5: The changing dynamics in online retail and industrial property are likely to impact investment strategies in several ways. Investors may need to reassess the long-term value and demand for large distribution facilities as online retail growth stabilizes and technology enables more efficient use of existing spaces. There could be a shift towards smaller, more flexible industrial spaces or multi-use properties that can adapt to changing market needs. At the same time, the renewed interest in brick-and-mortar shopping might make retail properties more attractive. Investors may need to diversify their portfolios and consider a mix of industrial, retail, and potentially hybrid properties to mitigate risks and capitalize on evolving market trends.

Ray White Head of Research, Vanessa Rader, said the proportion of online retail sales has remained static over the past 18 months, raising questions about future demand for industrial facilities. "The growth trajectory of online shopping has paused, with consumers returning to brick-and-mortar stores, particularly for food and groceries," Ms Rader said. Online transactions now account for 10.9 per cent of all retail sales across the country, down from 15 per cent during the COVID peak. The industrial property sector was a standout performer during the pandemic, with large distribution facilities attracting significant institutional investment. Over $9 billion in industrial assets changed hands in the year to March 2022, leading to fierce competition and sharp declines in investment yields. However, the landscape is now changing, with advancements in technology potentially impacting space requirements. "AI-driven efficiencies, multi-level racking systems optimising space, and increased automation suggest that additional capacity could be absorbed within existing industrial footprints," Ms Rader said. The past 18 months have seen a slowdown in large industrial transactions, with changing financing costs contributing to rising yields and some land value declines across the country. "Despite persistently low vacancies, rents have levelled off, and new supply has been limited due to high construction costs further dampening investment demand," she said. Ms Rader suggested these developments could signal a significant shift in the industrial property landscape . "As logistics demand potentially wanes, the status of large distribution facilities may shift," she said. The renewed preference for brick-and-mortar shopping could bring stock back to stores, potentially energising retail assets across the country.[Hhow Australia's industrial property market is consolidating](/articles/australias-industrial-property-market-shifts-from-expansion-to-strategic-consolidation/). This shift in consumer behaviour and technological advancements may reshape the industrial property sector, with investors and developers adapting to changing market dynamics. ### Further questions {frontmatter.faqAnswer1} {frontmatter.faqAnswer2} {frontmatter.faqAnswer3} {frontmatter.faqAnswer4} {frontmatter.faqAnswer5}

## Property market set for growth in 2025, stronger gains in 2026

URL: https://attainloans.com.au/articles/property-market-set-for-growth-in-2025/

Description: Australian property prices are forecast to continue their upward trajectory over the next two years

Metadata:
- subTitle: Australian property prices are forecast to continue their upward trajectory over the next two years
- pubDate: Thu Jan 30 2025 00:00:00 GMT+0000 (Coordinated Universal Time)
- ogImage: [object Object]
- pageImage: [object Object]
- dcSubject: Australian property market, housing forecast, property prices, KPMG, real estate outlook, house prices, unit prices, property investment, rental market, affordability, interest rates, capital cities, Melbourne property, Sydney property, Perth property, property growth, market trends, residential property
- dcDescription: Australian property prices are forecast to continue their upward trajectory over the next two years, with the intriguing prospect of unit prices outpacing houses as affordability constraints reshape buyer behaviour, according to new market analysis.
- tags: Property-finance
- author: Chrystal Evans
- authorUrl: /about/
- pngUrl: x.png
- imageHeight: 250
- imageWidth: 199
- faqTitle1: Which Australian cities are expected to see the strongest property price growth in 2025 and 2026?
- faqAnswer1: According to KPMG's latest forecast, Perth is expected to lead house price growth in 2025 with a 4% increase, followed by Canberra and Melbourne (both 3.5%), and Sydney (3.3%). For 2026, Sydney is projected to take the top spot with 7.8% growth, followed by Melbourne (6%) and Brisbane (5.6%). In the unit market, Sydney and Perth are both forecast to see 5% growth in 2025, while Melbourne is expected to lead in 2026 with a substantial 7.1% increase. These projections reflect varying local market conditions, with factors such as supply constraints, population growth, and economic fundamentals influencing each city's performance. The forecasts suggest a potential recovery for Melbourne's property market after underperforming in recent years, while Perth continues to benefit from strong interstate migration and limited housing supply.
- faqTitle2: Why are unit prices expected to outpace house prices over the next two years?
- faqAnswer2: Unit prices are forecast to outpace house prices primarily due to affordability constraints pushing buyers toward more accessible housing options. With the median house price in major capitals reaching prohibitive levels for many buyers, apartments and townhouses represent a more viable entry point to the property market. KPMG projects unit prices to rise by 4.6% in 2025 and 5.5% in 2026, compared to house price growth of 3.3% and 6% respectively. This shift also reflects limited new unit approvals in recent years, creating supply constraints that put upward pressure on existing unit prices. Additionally, changing lifestyle preferences and the desire for proximity to amenities are driving interest in well-located attached dwellings. For investors, units typically offer better rental yields than houses, further supporting demand in this segment. This trend marks a significant shift in market dynamics that could persist if housing affordability continues to challenge potential buyers.
- faqTitle3: What factors could influence the property market's performance over the next two years?
- faqAnswer3: Several key factors will influence property market performance through 2025-2026. Interest rates remain perhaps the most critical variable, with forecast cuts expected to begin around mid-2025 potentially stimulating buyer activity and confidence. Supply constraints continue to underpin price growth, though recent improvements in building approvals may gradually ease pressure if these translate to completed dwellings. Population trends will play a significant role, with overseas migration expected to normalise from recent peaks but remain historically strong. Rental market dynamics are another important factor, as moderating rental growth (forecast at 3.5-4.5% annually) may reduce the pressure on renters to become buyers. Economic conditions, including unemployment rates and wage growth, will influence borrowing capacity and market confidence. Lending policies, government housing initiatives, and investor sentiment will also shape market activity. Global economic conditions and potential regulatory changes add further variables to the outlook, highlighting the complexity of property market forecasting.
- faqTitle4: How does the latest forecast compare to actual property performance in 2024?
- faqAnswer4: The latest KPMG forecast suggests more moderate growth in 2025 compared to 2024, with national house prices projected to rise 3.3% (down from 5.1% in 2024) before accelerating to 6% in 2026. Unit price growth is expected to remain relatively consistent, with 4.6% forecast for 2025 compared to 4.5% achieved in 2024, before increasing to 5.5% in 2026. Interestingly, KPMG's previous forecasts proved quite accurate, having predicted 5.3% house price growth and 4.5% unit growth for 2024 (against actual results of 5.1% and 4.5% respectively). This suggests their modelling has successfully captured key market dynamics. The forecast for 2025-2026 indicates a market that remains resilient but is responding to affordability constraints, with growth expected to strengthen in the latter half of 2025 as interest rate cuts potentially begin. Overall, while the immediate outlook shows some moderation, the medium-term forecast remains positive, particularly for 2026 when more substantial gains are anticipated.
- faqTitle5: What's the outlook for the rental market over the next two years?
- faqAnswer5: The rental market is expected to see a welcome moderation after the significant increases of recent years. KPMG forecasts annual rental growth to ease to between 3.5% and 4.5% over 2025-2026, down from the peak of 7.8% recorded in March 2024 and the 6.7% rate observed in September 2024. This moderation reflects normalising migration patterns from the recent boom and gradually improving housing supply as more investor properties enter the market. The forecast represents a significant cooling from recent highs but remains above the long-term historical average for rental growth. Vacancy rates are expected to gradually improve from the extremely tight levels seen in 2023-2024, though they will likely remain below pre-pandemic levels in most markets. - faqTitle1: What is a bridging loan and how does it work in Australia?
- faqAnswer1: A bridging loan is a short-term finance solution that allows you to buy a new property before selling your existing one. It works by using the equity in your current home as security to fund the purchase of your new property. The loan typically lasts 6-12 months, during which you hold both properties. When your original property sells, the proceeds pay off the bridging loan, and any remaining balance converts to a standard home loan. Most lenders offer interest-only repayments or capitalised interest during the bridging period, meaning you might not make repayments until your property sells. The structure usually involves two accounts: the bridging loan itself and the 'end debt' which becomes your ongoing mortgage.
- faqTitle2: What are the current bridging loan interest rates in Australia for 2025?
- faqAnswer2: Bridging loan interest rates in Australia typically start from around 6.00% per annum, though some lenders offer rates as low as 5% for borrowers with strong equity positions. However, bridging loans generally carry higher rates than standard home loans. For instance, if a regular home loan is 5.00% per annum, bridging loan rates might range between 8-9% per annum. This reflects the short-term nature and higher risk profile of bridging finance. Rates vary between lenders based on your equity position, loan amount, property types, and overall risk assessment. With interest rates falling throughout 2025 following RBA cuts, some bridging loan rates may become more competitive, but they typically remain higher than standard mortgage rates due to their temporary nature.
- faqTitle3: Who is eligible for bridging finance and what are the requirements?
- faqAnswer3: Bridging loan eligibility requires several key criteria. You need substantial equity in your current property, typically around 50% equity minimum, though some lenders accept 20% equity (80% loan-to-value ratio). Lenders assess the likelihood that your current property will sell within the bridging period, often favouring urban properties in established markets over remote or unique properties. You must demonstrate capacity to service interest-only payments on combined debt during the bridging period. Income verification, asset statements, property valuations, and credit history checks are required. Some lenders require cash savings equivalent to expected interest charges. Additionally, you need a realistic exit strategy for selling your current property, and some lenders may require a confirmed contract for your new property purchase before approval.
- faqTitle4: What are the main risks and disadvantages of bridging loans?
- faqAnswer4: The primary risk of bridging loans is carrying substantial short-term debt on both properties simultaneously for 6-12 months. This creates exposure to higher interest costs, especially if your property takes longer to sell than expected. Bridging loans carry higher interest rates than standard home loans, typically 2-4% above regular mortgage rates. Market timing presents another risk - if property values decline or market conditions soften, you might face challenges selling within the bridging period or achieving expected sale prices. There's also refinancing risk if you can't sell within the term and need to renegotiate or convert to full repayments on the larger loan amount. Documentation and approval processes can be complex, and not all lenders offer bridging finance, potentially limiting your options.
- faqTitle5: Is bridging finance worth it in the current Australian property market?
- faqAnswer5: Bridging finance can be valuable in 2025's competitive Australian property market, particularly with falling interest rates and continued property price growth forecast. The strategy works best if you have strong equity (50%+ in current property), stable income, and realistic selling timeline expectations. Benefits include avoiding $8,300 average relocation costs, preventing temporary displacement (52% of sell-first buyers need temporary accommodation), and securing properties in competitive markets where unconditional offers are preferred. However, it's not suitable for everyone - you must be comfortable with higher short-term debt and interest costs. The decision depends on weighing convenience and market timing advantages against additional borrowing costs. Professional guidance from mortgage brokers and property advisors helps determine if bridging finance aligns with your specific circumstances and local market conditions.

A bridging loan is essentially a short-term financial bridge between two major property transactions. These specialised home loans allow you to access the equity in your current property to fund the purchase of a new home before your existing property sells. Think of it as temporary finance that keeps you moving forward while your property sale catches up. ### Loan structure and terms Bridging loans typically operate for terms of 6 to 12 months, giving you breathing space to sell your current home without the pressure of rushed timelines. The structure usually involves two loan accounts: the bridging loan itself (which is paid off when your current property sells) and the 'end debt' (which converts to your ongoing mortgage after settlement). ### Current rates and borrowing capacity Current bridging loan interest rates in Australia typically start from around 6.00% per annum, though some lenders may offer rates in the 5% range for borrowers with strong equity positions. This global context influences Australia's monetary policy decisions, particularly given its impact on exchange rates and international trade. ### What to expect The RBA has been careful to manage expectations about future rate movements. While this cut represents a significant shift, the central bank emphasises that monetary policy remains restrictive and will continue to be so. This suggests that while further cuts may be possible, they are likely to be gradual and data-dependent. Market analysts are forecasting a measured easing cycle through 2025, with most predicting the cash rate to settle between 3.35 and 3.85 percent by year's end. However, these projections remain highly dependent on incoming economic data, particularly inflation readings and labor market statistics. The rate cut is expected to have varying effects across different sectors of the economy: * Housing Market: The reduction in borrowing costs could provide support to property prices, though affordability constraints remain significant. * Consumer Spending: Lower mortgage payments may free up household budgets, potentially supporting retail spending. * Business Investment: Reduced borrowing costs could encourage business expansion, though uncertainty about future economic conditions may temper this effect. * Financial Markets: The Australian dollar may face some downward pressure, while bond markets adjust to the new rate environment. While the rate cut represents positive progress in managing inflation, several risks remain. The RBA is particularly concerned about the possibility that easing policy too quickly could stall the disinflation process. Additionally, global uncertainties, including geopolitical tensions and international trade dynamics, continue to pose risks to the economic outlook. [How to structure your home loan after a rate cut](/articles/what-rising-prices-mean-for-your-home-loan-strategy-in-2026/). The RBA's decision-making process remains firmly anchored to incoming economic data. Key indicators that will influence future decisions include: * Quarterly inflation readings * Monthly labor market statistics * Measures of consumer spending and business confidence * Global economic developments * Wage growth indicators * Productivity measures The February rate, while providing welcome relief to [home loan borrowers](/services/property/home-loans/), also signals the RBA's growing confidence in the inflation outlook. However, the central bank's cautious approach suggests a careful balancing act will continue, ensuring that inflation returns sustainably to target while supporting economic growth. - faqTitle3: What government assistance is available for first home buyers in Victoria in 2025
- faqAnswer3: Victorian first home buyers access multiple layers of government support that can reduce entry costs by tens of thousands of dollars. The stamp duty exemption provides the largest benefit, completely eliminating duty on properties valued up to $600,000 and offering concessions on properties between $600,001 and $750,000. For a $600,000 property, this exemption saves approximately $31,070 in upfront costs that would otherwise require cash payment at settlement. The First Home Owner Grant delivers $10,000 to eligible buyers purchasing or building new homes valued up to $750,000. This grant applies only to new properties including house and land packages, newly built apartments, and newly constructed houses. The property must be genuinely new, never previously occupied. While the $750,000 cap limits availability for houses in inner suburbs, many first home buyers successfully access this grant for units, townhouses, and house and land packages in outer suburbs and regional areas. The First Home Guarantee Scheme, a federal initiative, allows eligible buyers to purchase with just a 5% deposit without paying Lenders Mortgage Insurance. From October 2025, this scheme offers unlimited places with no income restrictions. In Melbourne and Geelong, the property cap sits at $950,000, while regional Victoria has a $600,000 cap. LMI typically costs $10,000 to $30,000 depending on loan size, so avoiding this fee provides significant savings. The scheme applies to new, established, and off-the-plan properties. Income limits and property value caps apply to these schemes, so buyers should verify eligibility before committing to purchases. Some schemes can be combined. For example, a first home buyer purchasing a new townhouse valued at $700,000 could potentially access the stamp duty concession, the $10,000 First Home Owner Grant, and the First Home Guarantee Scheme to purchase with 5% deposit and no LMI. Working with mortgage brokers who specialise in first home buyer lending helps maximise these benefits while ensuring loan structures suit long-term financial goals. Attain Loans provides expertise in navigating these schemes and structuring applications to optimise outcomes for Victorian first home buyers.

- faqTitle5: How do Victoria's new land tax changes affect property investment decisions
- faqAnswer5: The 2024 Victorian land tax changes fundamentally altered investment property economics, prompting many investors to reassess Victorian holdings. The government lowered the land tax free threshold from $300,000 to $50,000 and introduced additional flat-rate levies on investment properties. For investors, this means properties that previously incurred no land tax now generate annual tax obligations. A typical investment property with land valued at $650,000 now incurs approximately $1,300 more in annual land tax compared to the previous regime. This amount might seem modest in isolation, but it directly reduces net rental returns and cash flow. For investors holding multiple properties, the cumulative impact becomes substantial. A portfolio of three investment properties might see annual land tax increases of $3,000 to $5,000, meaningfully affecting investment viability. Compare Victoria's $50,000 threshold to New South Wales at $1,075,000 or Queensland at $600,000, and the relative disadvantage becomes stark. An investment property in Brisbane with land valued at $500,000 incurs zero land tax, while an identical investment in Melbourne generates several thousand dollars in annual tax. This disparity explains why approximately 5,000 more investors sold Victorian properties following the announcement compared to other states. Some investors exited the Victorian market entirely, redeploying capital to Queensland, New South Wales, or regional Victoria where thresholds remain higher. Others accepted reduced returns, viewing the tax as a cost of accessing Melbourne's long-term growth potential. The strategic question for investors is whether Melbourne's counter-cyclical opportunity offsets the increased holding costs. Buying near a market low while competitors flee could generate capital gains that dwarf annual tax costs. A property purchased at $800,000 that appreciates to $1 million over five years generates $200,000 in capital gain, easily offsetting $6,500 to $10,000 in additional land tax over that period. Regional Victoria offers a compromise, with many regional properties falling below land tax thresholds while offering superior rental yields compared to Melbourne. Investors should model total returns including projected capital growth, rental yields, and all holding costs including the new land tax regime. For some investors, Melbourne remains viable. For others, interstate or regional alternatives offer better risk-adjusted returns. Working with accountants and buyers agents who understand these dynamics helps investors make informed decisions aligned with their portfolio strategies and risk tolerance.

Many borrowers choose split loans, fixing a portion for certainty while keeping some funds variable for flexibility. Maximising borrowing capacity with stable rates requires understanding how lenders assess serviceability. Most lenders add buffers to current rates when calculating maximum borrowing capacity, meaning the actual rate you pay differs from the rate used for serviceability calculations. First home buyer schemes provide substantial benefits but require navigating complex eligibility criteria. These work well for specific bookings but don't provide comprehensive travel funding. ### Australian travel trends driving loan demand in 2025 Australian travel patterns in 2025 reflect both pent-up demand from previous restrictions and evolving preferences that drive travel loan usage. #### Rising spending and confidence Despite cost of living pressures, travel remains a priority for Australians, with 43% planning to travel more in 2025. The data shows that 36% of Australians plan to spend more on flights, 31% on accommodation, and 14% on car hire in 2025. This increased spending, combined with limited savings capacity for many households, creates ideal conditions for travel loan demand. Aussies are spending more on summer holidays with an average of $4,602, exceeding spending in the US ($4,544), Canada ($3,633), and Europe ($3,144). This higher spending level often exceeds readily available savings, making structured financing through travel loans attractive. #### Destination preferences and booking patterns According to [Skyscanner's Travel Trends 2025 report](https: The top experiences and factors determining Aussie travellers' choice of destination are weather (66%), attractions (65%), food (63%), and culture (59%). Younger Australians (18-24) are most likely to travel overseas, with 58% planning international trips. More than 40% of Australians book international holidays 1-6 months in advance, while 35% book 6-12 months ahead. This relatively short planning horizon often doesn't align with savings accumulation timelines, supporting travel loan usage for optimal booking timing. ### How to apply for a travel loan: Step-by-step process Applying for a holiday loan is much like applying for any unsecured personal loan, but strategic planning ensures you secure the best terms while borrowing responsibly. #### Budget planning and loan sizing First, figure out your holiday budget and how much you'll need to borrow. Detailed budgeting prevents over-borrowing and reduces total interest costs. Research destination-specific costs, seasonal price variations, and potential currency fluctuations. Include contingency funds for unexpected expenses or opportunities that arise during travel. Consider supplementing loan amounts with existing savings. The less money you borrow, the less you'll pay in interest and fees over the loan term. Many successful travel loan users combine loans for major upfront costs (flights, accommodation) with savings for daily expenses and discretionary spending. #### Application process and requirements Once you've got your budget, you can talk with a finance broker who can compare your options. They will be able to find a suitable product to meet your travel needs. The application process typically involves: - **Documentation gathering**: Proof of income, employment verification, bank statements, and identification - **Credit assessment**: Lenders evaluate your credit history, existing obligations, and repayment capacity - **Loan structure selection**: Choose between fixed or variable rates, repayment frequency, and loan terms - **Approval and funding**: Most lenders provide decisions within 24-48 hours, with funds available shortly after approval Eligibility criteria vary between lenders but generally require Australian residency, minimum income levels (often $25,000+ annually), and satisfactory credit history. Age limits typically range from 18 to 65-70 years depending on the lender. #### Timing and booking strategies Apply for travel loans when promotional fares and accommodation deals are available rather than waiting for perfect savings accumulation. Many travellers benefit from securing loans during airline sales periods or hotel promotional campaigns. ### Responsible borrowing: Risks and considerations While travel loans provide valuable flexibility, responsible borrowing requires careful assessment of your financial capacity and travel planning. #### Financial impact assessment Evaluate your ability to service loan repayments comfortably alongside existing obligations. Travel loans typically require immediate repayment commencement, unlike some other personal loans that offer repayment deferrals. Consider the loan's impact on your credit profile and future borrowing capacity. Multiple credit applications within short periods can negatively affect credit scores, so research options thoroughly before applying rather than submitting multiple applications. Assess your employment stability and income consistency. Travel loan terms typically span 1-7 years, requiring confidence in your ability to maintain repayments throughout this period. [Financing other major purchases with a personal loan](/articles/can-you-finance-your-wedding/). #### Interest and fee considerations Compare total borrowing costs beyond headline interest rates. Many travel loans include establishment fees, monthly account-keeping fees, and potential early repayment penalties. Some lenders offer fee-free products that may carry slightly higher rates but lower total costs for shorter-term borrowing. Calculate total repayment amounts over different loan terms. Longer terms reduce monthly payments but increase total interest costs, while shorter terms save money overall but require higher monthly commitments. Many lenders offer early repayment options without penalties, enabling borrowers to reduce interest costs if additional funds become available during the loan term. #### Travel insurance and protection planning Most travel loan lenders recommend or require comprehensive travel insurance to protect both borrower and lender interests. Quality travel insurance covers trip cancellations, medical emergencies, and other events that could affect repayment capacity. Some travel loans integrate with specific travel insurance products or offer discounted insurance through partner providers. Evaluate these offerings against independent insurance options to ensure adequate coverage at competitive prices. Plan for potential trip modifications or cancellations. Understanding your rights and obligations if travel plans change helps avoid financial stress and protects your credit standing. ### Making the decision: Is a travel loan right for you? Travel loans suit specific financial situations and travel goals, but they're not appropriate for everyone. Careful evaluation ensures you make the best choice for your circumstances. #### Financial readiness assessment Evaluate your income stability, existing debt obligations, and cash flow capacity. Travel loans work best for borrowers with steady employment, manageable debt levels, and sufficient income to service additional repayments comfortably. Consider your savings rate and timeline. If you can reasonably save your target travel budget within 3-6 months, paying cash might be more economical than borrowing. However, if saving requires 12+ months, travel loans might enable better timing and deals. Assess your credit profile and likely interest rates. Borrowers with excellent credit access the most competitive rates, making travel loans more attractive. Those with average or poor credit might face higher rates that reduce the value proposition. #### Travel timing and planning considerations Evaluate your travel flexibility and timing requirements. Travel loans provide most value when specific timing is important - seasonal destinations, limited-time offers, or special events that can't be delayed for savings accumulation. Consider destination costs and currency factors. Travel loans work particularly well for expensive destinations where significant upfront costs are required, or when currency movements favour early booking over delayed purchases. Assess group travel dynamics and family considerations. Travel loans can facilitate group bookings that secure better rates or ensure availability for family trips where coordination is complex. #### Alternative strategy evaluation Compare travel loan costs against other options. ## Should you choose principal and interest from day one
